root_cause.text: In KVM/arm64, `__kvm_at_s12()` and `__kvm_find_s1_desc_level()` performed guest page-table walks via `kvm_walk_nested_s2()` and `walk_s1()` without holding `vcpu->kvm->srcu`, leaving those walks unprotected against concurrent memslot changes.
root_cause.evidence: The patch explicitly says `walk_s1()` and `kvm_walk_nested_s2()` “expect to be called while holding kvm->srcu to guard against memslot changes,” but notes that `__kvm_at_s12()` and `__kvm_find_s1_desc_level()` called them “without taking kvm->srcu”; the diff fixes this by wrapping both calls in `scoped_guard(srcu, &vcpu->kvm->srcu)`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Protect the nested stage-2 walk with SRCU to avoid concurrent access races in KVM translation handling.
intent_record.what: The direct call to `kvm_walk_nested_s2(vcpu, ipa, &out)` was wrapped inside a `scoped_guard(srcu, &vcpu->kvm->srcu)` block, so the function now executes under an SRCU read-side protection scope.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this ensures the nested stage-2 walk is performed while the KVM SRCU lock is held, protecting access to KVM state from concurrent teardown or mutation and preventing races during the translation walk.

intent_record.intent_summary: Protect the guest stage-1 page table walk with KVM SRCU to avoid races during descriptor lookup.
intent_record.what: The call to `walk_s1(vcpu, &wi, &wr, va)` is wrapped in a `scoped_guard(srcu, &vcpu->kvm->srcu)` block, so the guest page table walk now executes under the KVM SRCU read-side protection.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this ensures the walk cannot race with concurrent SRCU-protected teardown or updates of the KVM data structures it depends on, making the guest page table lookup safe against use-after-free or inconsistent traversal during the walk.

relevance_review.reason: The group explicitly adds SRCU protection around the nested stage-2 walk, which matches the root cause: unprotected guest page-table walks in KVM arm64 due to missing vcpu->kvm->srcu during walk operations.

The group directly matches the root cause: it adds KVM SRCU protection around guest stage-1 page-table walks used during descriptor lookup, which addresses the missing synchronization against concurrent memslot changes.

candidates.rationale: This is the guest stage-2 page-table walk performed without any SRCU protection, which matches the root cause of unsafe nested walks during concurrent memslot changes.
This is the guest stage-1 page-table walk performed without holding vcpu->kvm->srcu, directly exposing the descriptor lookup to races with concurrent memslot updates.

vuln_statements.explanation: This guest stage-2 page-table walk was executed without holding vcpu->kvm->srcu, allowing concurrent memslot changes to race with nested translation.
This guest stage-1 page-table walk was performed without KVM SRCU protection, exposing descriptor lookup to races during concurrent memslot updates.
